Hans Hack

or how I hacked the Hans Haacke show at the New Museum after they union-busted their employees

2020
Performance intervention, institutional critique

While the New Museum was exhibiting a retrospective of Hans Haacke, an artist known for exposing the politics of the institutions that show him, it hired a union-busting firm to deal with its organizing employees. The exhibition included a new work, a survey polling visitors about their politics, and, unsurprisingly, it reported a fairly liberal public in support of progressive politics. In solidarity with the museum workers, and against the use of radical art for profit while workers are exploited, the artist hacked the survey results so that they more accurately reflected the politics of the museum itself.
